title: How often a cylinder sheds vortices
question: A long circular cylinder lies across a steady, uniform stream of air at low speed. Above a Reynolds number of about 40 it sheds vortices alternately from its two sides. Report the shedding frequency as a Strouhal number St = f d / U at each Reynolds number Re = U d / nu.

conditions.fluid: air at low speed (incompressible), low free-stream turbulence (a wind tunnel)
conditions.body: circular cylinders of several diameters, long compared with their diameter, spanning the tunnel
conditions.correction: the measurements are corrected for tunnel blockage (unbounded flow is asked for); end effects were not corrected
conditions.measurement: hot-wire anemometry in the wake, frequencies from Lissajous figures

outputs.name: strouhal
outputs.meaning: f d / U, f the shedding frequency of one side

label: T1
subtitle: Leads to flag 01 · the Strouhal number from Re 60 to 145
